title: Tarka Dhal
subtitle: Yellow split lentils with cumin-tempered ghee
excerpt: Red lentils simmered to a creamy, thick soup, finished with a tarka of cumin seeds and garlic fried in ghee until sizzling. The tarka is added at the table and stirred in just before eating.

recipe.sourceNotes: Tarka dhal (also dal tadka) is one of the most widely eaten dishes across the Indian subcontinent. Tarka (or tadka/chaunk) refers to the technique of tempering whole spices in hot fat and pouring them over a dish as a finishing step. It is a cornerstone of everyday Indian home cooking.

content.text: Tarka dhal is one of the most forgiving and satisfying things in Indian cooking. The lentils simmer until completely soft and creamy, almost porridge-like, and the tarka, whole cumin seeds, dried chilli, and sliced garlic fried in ghee until golden, is poured over the top at the last moment. The sizzle when the hot ghee hits the lentils is part of the dish.

Put the rinsed lentils in a large saucepan with 1 litre of cold water and the turmeric. Bring to a boil, skim off any foam, then reduce the heat and simmer uncovered for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils have completely dissolved into a thick, creamy soup. Add salt and stir.

While the lentils cook, heat 1 tablespoon of the ghee in a separate pan over medium heat. Add the diced onion and cook for 10 to 12 minutes until soft and golden. Add the ginger and cook for 2 more minutes. Add the tinned tomatoes and simmer for 5 minutes until thickened. Stir this mixture into the cooked lentils along with the garam masala.

For the tarka: heat the remaining 2 tablespoons of ghee in a small frying pan over high heat until it shimmers. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 30 seconds. Add the sliced garlic and dried chillies. Fry, stirring, for 1 to 2 minutes until the garlic is golden but not burnt.

Pour the hot tarka directly over the surface of the dhal. It will sizzle. Scatter over the fresh coriander and serve immediately with rice or flatbreads, letting everyone stir the tarka through at the table.
